clue.text: Book place and sign on line

blocks.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY, short for railway, is a common crossword abbreviation for a line

explanation.surface: Instructions for registering a reservation: put your book down and sign on the dotted line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply means the sign is placed before the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a building where books are kept and borrowed, hence a place for books.

clue.text: Tremendous, when single chaps embrace married state's limits

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece is held inside another
a word's limits are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the abbreviation for married
chaps are men
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bachelors hugging a married couple at the edges of a vast state — or the joy of single men settling down.
explanation.walkthrough: I and MEN together are the single chaps, and they take M inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, a synonym of tremendous in its sense of enormous.

clue.text: M25, say, has mechanism for carriageway repairs

blocks.note: the M25 is the orbital motorway round London, an example of a road
the works of a clock are its mechanism

explanation.surface: The London ring road has gear for fixing its surface — as drivers stuck in traffic know.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadworks are the repairs and construction carried out on a road, causing lane closures.

clue.text: Cyclical work timetable has disheartened Rosemary

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle goes, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: a rota is a schedule of who works when
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rosemary is fed up because the shift schedule keeps going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes motion turning round in a circle, i.e. repeating in cycles.

clue.text: Doctor means to take contents of vial for memory loss

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
the contents of a word are its inner letters, with the outer ones discarded

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A medic prescribing something from a little bottle to treat forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person treating the patient, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange MEANS once it takes in IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total inability to remember.

clue.text: Encourage to provide Vimto and tea

indicators.note: to provide something here is to make it out of the given materials, rearranging them

blocks.note: Vimto is a British fruit-flavoured soft drink; the two words without the 'and'

explanation.surface: Offering drinks to cheer someone on.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak; the fodder's letters are simply rearranged to form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To motivate someone is to spur them on, giving them reason to act, i.e. to encourage.

clue.text: Come into some barren terrain

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them is used, running across the gap

blocks.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: Wandering onto a stretch of barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into a place is to go inside it, which is what entering means.

clue.text: No way out with these in the house?

definitions.text: No way out with these in the house?

blocks.clueFragment: No way out with these in the house?
blocks.note: surface reading: a house with no exits, so you are trapped
setter's reading: the answer splits as a word for inside plus the things that let you out of a house

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as IN plus a word for exits: without the exits you are stuck inside, and the whole word means within the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes being within a building, under a roof rather than outside.

clue.text: One's hoping for a good deal from pub with hunting era style

definitions.text: One's hoping for a good deal

indicators.note: to style something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub decked out in old-fashioned hunting gear, hoping to get a cheap pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain hunter searches shops for goods at low prices, wanting value for money.

clue.text: One politician has skill to communicate

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Member of Parliament
an art is a skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A single politician who is gifted at getting a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on, a synonym for communicating it.

clue.text: Pose with a model bird due to fly

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous early car
a tit is a small songbird
rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion model striking a pose, with a bird about to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pose' and 'model' together suggest a photo shoot, but 'model' is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a posture of the body, as when a dancer or model strikes one.

clue.text: Blow the cobwebs away with song

blocks.note: first meaning: to freshen a room by letting a breeze through
second meaning: a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Clearing your head by singing a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a room is to ventilate it, and an air is also a simple melody.

clue.text: Article points us to right solution

blocks.note: the indefinite article
three compass points: south, west, east
the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A newspaper article steering readers to the correct solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' supplies more than one compass point here: three of them in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to a puzzle is its solution, the two words being straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Chief justice minister's car keeps on coming back

indicators.note: something coming back retraces its path, so the word reads in the opposite direction
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Michael Gove was the UK Justice Secretary in 2015-16
a Rolls-Royce, abbreviated
taken as written, then turned around

explanation.surface: The top judge and a government minister disagree about a car that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief justice' reads as one title, but 'Chief' alone is the definition; the minister's car is a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is the person in charge of an institution or colony, its head or boss.

clue.text: Crossing place for African animal?

blocks.note: first meaning: a striped pedestrian crossing on a British road
second meaning: a striped wild horse of the savannah

explanation.surface: A spot where African wildlife can safely cross.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pedestrian crossing painted with black and white stripes is called by the name of the striped animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped beast of the African plains lends its name to the striped British road crossing.

clue.text: Silly twit in charge is initially mystified by repartee

indicators.note: something silly is all over the place, so its letters are muddled
initially points to the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: rearranged
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge
taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish boss is baffled by someone else's quick retorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is clever, witty banter, and a single witticism is one such clever remark.

clue.text: Study question and make mistake about old king's title

indicators.note: to go about something is to go around it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a standard abbreviation for question
to err is to make a mistake
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A history student investigates and gets a medieval monarch's name wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: William the Conqueror was the Norman king who took England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: William I of England is known by this epithet, the title added to his name.

clue.text: Quick meal in Kentish Town

blocks.note: first meaning: bread with a filling
second meaning: a historic port in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Grabbing a bite in Kentish Town, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a London district, but here it means a town in the county of Kent, whose Earl gave his title to the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The snack of bread and filling is named after the Earl of Sandwich, from the Kent town.

clue.text: Have to admit zero pain from growth on lip

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: must means have to
the figure 0 looks like the letter
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Having to confess you feel no pain from a cold sore on your lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is hair grown on the upper lip, so a growth there in a hairy sense.

clue.text: Go on too long and micro-manage?

blocks.note: first meaning: to exceed the time allotted
second meaning, read cryptically

explanation.surface: A meeting that drags on because the boss interferes in every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as playful: to run something excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that overruns exceeds its scheduled time; split, the word suggests running things to excess.

clue.text: Put last bun in bag — it will keep you going until mealtime

definitions.text: it will keep you going until mealtime

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
put ... in tells you to place one piece inside another

blocks.note: a sack is a large bag
final letter

explanation.surface: Packing the leftover bun into your bag to tide you over until lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack is a small amount of food eaten between meals to stave off hunger.

clue.text: Split with church over king's depravity

indicators.note: the church covers the king, spreading over him on both sides

blocks.note: the Church of England
R for rex, Latin for king
vice is moral depravity

explanation.surface: A schism in the church over a monarch's wicked behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a church schism, but it is a noun for a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or fissure in rock or a wall, i.e. a split.

clue.text: Understand obese Frenchman losing condition

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from what remains

blocks.note: fat means obese
French for man
ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is a medical condition

explanation.surface: An overweight Frenchman getting over an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, i.e. to comprehend it fully.

clue.text: Checked reported noise from shower?

indicators.note: a reported noise is something heard, so the spelling follows how the phrase is said

blocks.note: a rain shower that came indoors

explanation.surface: Checking out a strange sound coming from the bathroom shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' looks like inspecting the noise, but it means restrained, as a rider pulls on reins.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or one's spending is to restrain or curb it, i.e. to check it.

clue.text: Northern wild rice is tastier

indicators.note: something wild is unruly, so its letters run out of order

blocks.note: the abbreviation for northern
rearranged

explanation.surface: A northerner's opinion that wild rice beats the ordinary kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild rice' looks like the grain, but 'wild' is telling you to mix up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer, used of food, means more pleasant to eat, so tastier.

clue.text: When letter from Athens comes in, editor's kept busy

indicators.note: a thing that comes in enters, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor swamped with work when a letter arrives from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to occupy or entertain them, keeping them busy and diverted.

clue.text: Sound disapproving of short ballet dress

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final part

blocks.note: a tutu is a ballerina's stiff skirt

explanation.surface: Clicking your tongue at a ballerina's skimpy skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is the clicking sound people make to show mild disapproval or annoyance.

clue.text: Rehearse scene in lift

indicators.note: one thing in another is held within it

blocks.note: to prise something is to lever it up
a scene and an act are both divisions of a play

explanation.surface: Running through a scene set in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: PRACTISE is the British spelling of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play or piece is to go over it repeatedly, i.e. to practise it.

clue.text: One wanting solitude gets it on small Channel Island

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another follows it, so the second piece comes after the first

blocks.note: Herm is one of the smallest of the Channel Islands, near Guernsey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loner finds peace by retreating to a tiny island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the island before IT; the Channel Islands lie off the coast of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is a recluse who lives apart from society, seeking to be alone.

clue.text: Canary flapping round her head causes chaos

indicators.note: a flapping bird is in a flurry, so its letters are thrown about and wrapped round the extra one
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter

explanation.surface: A pet canary fluttering about a woman's head throws the house into disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, so a synonym for chaos or confusion.

clue.text: Sniggered about girl and caused annoyance

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: Ms is the title used for a woman
to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: Someone laughed behind a girl's back and annoyed her.
explanation.definitionFit: To smirk is to smile in a smug, sneering way, close to sniggering in spirit.
